charges.title: Asynchronous State Race Condition
charges.description: When userId changes rapidly, promises resolve out of order. A slow network response for an earlier user will overwrite the state of a newer user on line 14.

charges.title: Uncancelled Async Subscription on Unmount
charges.description: The useEffect hook on lines 7-18 has no cleanup function returning an AbortController abort call, leading to memory leaks and unmounted component state updates.

charges.title: Permissive 'any' Type Annotation
charges.description: State is initialized with untyped 'any' on line 4, disabling TypeScript type checking across consumers of the hook.

debate.speaker: prosecutor
debate.text: Your Honor, observe line 14! If a user swiftly toggles between profile tabs, this hook experiences an uncontrolled race condition, displaying Profile B with the data of Profile A!

debate.speaker: defense
debate.text: The defense agrees that network delays may cause jitter, but this hook was structured for simplicity in a dashboard where user switching is rare.

debate.speaker: prosecutor
debate.text: Rare? When the user navigates away, line 17 leaves the promise dangling! React will scream console warnings regarding unmounted component updates and leaked memory.

debate.speaker: defense
debate.text: We are eager to implement an AbortController cleanup cycle, along with strict UserProfile interfaces. This code is salvageable!

debate.speaker: judge
debate.text: The Court recognizes that while no malicious breach occurred, unpredictable state logic and memory leaks cannot go unaddressed. A verdict with mandatory community service is appropriate.

verdict.summary: The Court finds the code GUILTY WITH COMMUNITY SERVICE. The implementation is benign in security intent but criminally negligent in asynchronous lifecycle hygiene and race condition mitigation.
sentence: Instantiate an AbortController inside useEffect and abort pending HTTP requests on component unmount.
Implement a boolean active flag or signal check to prevent out-of-order state settlement.
Replace 'any' with a dedicated UserProfile TypeScript interface.
Add try/catch or fetch rejection handling to account for aborted network requests without noisy console errors.

cannedObjections.trigger: React 18 automatically handles state updates safely during component unmounting!
cannedObjections.reply: React may suppress the red warning, but dangling network requests still consume client bandwidth and produce stale closure races.

cannedObjections.trigger: A debounce layer on the parent component prevents rapid userId switching!
cannedObjections.reply: Band-aids on consumer components do not forgive an inherently non-reentrant custom hook.

cannedObjections.trigger: Using AbortController natively cancels the HTTP request cleanly!
cannedObjections.reply: Sustained. Modern browser AbortController with an active cleanup closure represents the gold standard remedy.

improvements: Introduced AbortController with automatic teardown in useEffect cleanup function
Guarded against DOM state update race conditions when userId changes quickly
Added strict UserProfile TypeScript interface replacing 'any'
Handled AbortError gracefully without triggering false error states
